# Relay stage 2: Research Task: control-api-index-page Working directory: /tmp/nix-shell.XRSYe6/visual-relay/wt/fbb5c78605a5/plan-20260706172744/control-api-index-page ## Task input # Control API index page Serve a plain HTML index at the control server's root (`GET /`) that documents the API surface — a short purpose blurb, the list of routes, and the list of command names. The routes and command names are enumerated from the code that already defines them, never re-typed as literals in the page. The page uses no CSS and no JavaScript, and is written to be accessible (WCAG). ## Current state The app (`VisualRelay.App`, an Avalonia desktop app on .NET 10) runs an embedded localhost HTTP control server so scripts/agents can drive the GUI. Relevant code: - **`ControlServer.cs`** (`src/VisualRelay.App/Services/`) — binds a `System.Net.HttpListener` to `http://127.0.0.1:/` (loopback only; default port `8765`, see `ControlServerOptions.FromEnvironment`). It is the built-in .NET HTTP listener — there is **no ASP.NET/Kestrel, no routing framework, no static-file middleware, no `wwwroot`**. - **`ControlServer.Routing.cs`** → `RouteAsync` — the entire request surface. It is a hand-written `if`/`else` chain. In order: - an optional token gate: when `options.Token` is set, a request without a matching `X-VR-Token` header gets `401` **before any path dispatch** (so every path, including a new one, is gated when a token is configured); - `GET /health`, `GET /state`, `GET /screenshot` (optional `?path=`), `POST /command/{name}`; - a final fallthrough that returns `404 {"ok":false,"error":"not found"}`. **`GET /` hits this 404 today** — the root is free. - Responses are written by two helpers in this same file: `WriteJsonAsync` (sets `ContentType = "application/json"`, writes UTF-8 bytes, sets `ContentLength64`) and an inline `image/png` write for screenshots. There is **no HTML writer yet**. - **Command names already live in code, in two places** the page must reuse (do not re-type them): - `ControlApi.State.cs` → the `IcommandNames` array — the 15 `ICommand`-backed command names (`bootstrap`, `run-all`, `run-selected`, `resume`, `refresh`, `pause-toggle`, `archive-toggle`, `new-task`, `follow-running`, `start-backend`, `edit`, `rewrite-selected`, `cancel-rewrite`, `revert-rewrite`, `mark-done`). This same array already backs `BuildCommandsMap`. - `ControlApi.cs` → the `PropertyActions` array — the 7 property-backed actions (`select-task`, `boost-turns`, `open-folder`, `obsidian-scan`, `obsidian-bridge`, `select-activity-tab`, `select-detail-tab`). `ResolveCommand` (the `switch` in the same file) resolves the ICommand names; `InvokePropertyAction` handles the property actions. - **The four route paths are string literals inside `RouteAsync`** (`"/health"`, `"/state"`, `"/screenshot"`, the `"/command/"` prefix). There is no route table. Test conventions (`tests/VisualRelay.Tests/`, see `ControlServerTests.cs` and `ControlServerBodylessPostTests.cs`): - End-to-end server tests use `[Collection("Headless")]` on the class and `[AvaloniaFact]` on each test; they `new ControlServer(new ControlApi(vm, window), new ControlServerOptions(true, port, null))` on a free port (`GetFreePort()`), hit it with a shared `HttpClient`, assert status / content-type / body, and `server.Stop()` in a `finally`. - Pure logic (no UI thread, no listener) is tested with plain `[Fact]` (e.g. `ControlServerOptionsTests`). - There is a **~300-line-per-test-file guard** — keep new test files under it; split if needed. ## What to build ### 1. One source of truth for the surface (the "derive from code" requirement) - **Command names.** Add a public, ordered accessor on `ControlApi`, e.g. `public static IReadOnlyList CommandNames`, built by concatenating the **existing** `IcommandNames` and `PropertyActions` arrays (ICommand names first, then property actions). Do **not** introduce a third hand-typed list of command names anywhere. Adding a command to those arrays must automatically flow into this accessor (and therefore into the page). - **Routes.** Add one declarative route catalog — the single place the top-level surface is described — e.g. a `ControlRoutes` static class exposing `public static IReadOnlyList All`, where `RouteInfo` carries: the HTTP method, the canonical path used for matching (`/`, `/health`, `/state`, `/screenshot`, `/command/`), a human display form for parameterized routes (`/screenshot[?path=…]`, `/command/{name}`), and a one-line purpose summary. `RouteAsync` must **match against these catalog paths** (reference the catalog's path values instead of the bare string literals it uses today) so a route cannot exist in the router but be missing from the page, or vice versa. The catalog is what the page renders. ### 2. Root route, HTML writer, and renderer - In `RouteAsync`, add a `GET /` branch (before the `404` fallthrough) that renders and writes the index page. **Keep the token gate exactly where it is** — do not special-case `/`. Rationale: secure-by-default (a configured token protects the index too); the default no-token config still serves it to a browser. Any non-`GET` method on `/`, and any unknown path, keep falling through to the existing `404`. - Add a `WriteHtmlAsync` helper next to `WriteJsonAsync` in `ControlServer.Routing.cs`, mirroring it exactly but with `ContentType = "text/html; charset=utf-8"`. - Put the HTML generation in its own pure, static, UI-thread-free renderer so it can be unit-tested directly without spinning up a listener — e.g. `src/VisualRelay.App/Services/ControlIndexPage.cs` → `public static string Render(IReadOnlyList routes, IReadOnlyList commandNames)`. The root branch calls `ControlIndexPage.Render(ControlRoutes.All, ControlApi.CommandNames)`. HTML-encode every interpolated text/attribute value with `System.Net.WebUtility.HtmlEncode`. ### 3. Page content and structure (accessible, no CSS, no JavaScript) Emit a complete, valid HTML5 document. Target shape (structure fixed; the rows and list items are **generated by iterating the catalogs**, never hand-listed): ```html Visual Relay — Control API

Visual Relay Control API

The Visual Relay control API is a localhost-only HTTP surface for driving the running app the same way its on-screen buttons do: read live state, invoke commands, and capture screenshots. It exists so scripts and agents can automate and observe the GUI with no human at the keyboard. Every command maps to a real UI action and honors the same enabled/disabled gating as the corresponding button.

Endpoints

HTTP endpoints exposed by the control API
MethodPathPurpose

Commands

Invoke with POST /command/{name}. Available names:

``` Use the intro copy above **verbatim** (it is the purpose blurb — 3 sentences, no more). Accessibility requirements to satisfy: - ``; ``; ``; a descriptive ``. - Exactly one `<h1>`; section headings are `<h2>` with no skipped levels; content lives inside a `<main>` landmark; DOM order is the reading order. - The endpoints table has a `<caption>` and `<th scope="col">` column headers. - No color-conveyed meaning and no images; default black-on-white text meets contrast with no styling. ### 4. Hard constraints - **No CSS**: no `<style>`, no `<link rel="stylesheet">`, no `style=` attributes, no external stylesheet of any kind. - **No JavaScript**: no `<script>`, no `on…=` inline event-handler attributes, no `javascript:` URIs. ### 5. Docs - Update the control-API section of `AGENTS.md` (the block that lists `GET /health`, `GET /state`, `POST /command/{name}`, `GET /screenshot`) to add `GET /` → the HTML index page. ## Done when - `GET http://127.0.0.1:8765/` returns `200` with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and a valid HTML5 document; every other path still returns the existing `404`, and non-`GET` on `/` still `404`s. - When a token is configured, `GET /` without a matching `X-VR-Token` header returns `401` (it stays behind the existing gate); with the default no-token config it serves the page. - The page's endpoint rows are generated from `ControlRoutes.All` and its command list from `ControlApi.CommandNames`; **no route path or command name is hand-typed in `ControlIndexPage`.** `ControlApi.CommandNames` is composed from the existing `IcommandNames` + `PropertyActions` arrays. - The intro is the exact 3-sentence blurb above. - Accessibility: the document has `lang`, `charset`, a descriptive `<title>`, a single `<h1>` with ordered headings, a `<main>` landmark, and a table with `<caption>` + `scope="col"` headers. - Automated tests are added (new file `tests/VisualRelay.Tests/ControlIndexPageTests.cs`; if it would exceed the ~300-line guard, split server round-trip vs. renderer into two files): - **Pure renderer tests** (`[Fact]`, no Avalonia) over `ControlIndexPage.Render(...)`: - Derivation: the output contains every name in `ControlApi.CommandNames`, and every method + display path in `ControlRoutes.All`. (Adding a command/route without it appearing on the page fails the build.) - **No-CSS tripwire**: the rendered HTML contains none of these (case-insensitive) — `<style`, `<link`, `stylesheet`, and the attribute form ` style=` (a simple substring/`Regex ` style=`` check). Fails if CSS is introduced by tag or attribute. - **No-JavaScript tripwire**: the rendered HTML contains none of these (case-insensitive) — `<script`, `javascript:`, and any inline event-handler attribute (a simple ` on[a-z]+=` regex catches `onclick=`, `onload=`, etc.). Fails if JS is introduced by tag or attribute. - (These tripwires are deliberately simple regression guards, not exhaustive sanitizers.) - Structure: output contains `<!doctype html` (case-insensitive), `<html lang=`, a `<title>`, exactly one `<h1`, a `<main`, and the table's `<caption>` + `scope="col"`. - **End-to-end round-trip** (`[Collection("Headless")]` + `[AvaloniaFact]`, mirroring `ControlServerEndToEndTests`): start a `ControlServer` on a free port, `GET /`, assert `200`, `Content-Type` media type `text/html`, and a body beginning with `<!doctype html`. Add a token-configured variant asserting `GET /` without the header returns `401`. - The full test suite passes (`./test.sh`), including the existing `ControlServer*`/`ControlApi*` tests. ## Manifest (not set yet) ## Prior stages ## Stage 1 - Ideate { "summary": "Add a `GET /` HTML index page to the control server. Create `ControlApi.CommandNames` (composed from existing IcommandNames + PropertyActions) and a `ControlRoutes` catalog (the single source of truth for routes). Replace RouteAsync's bare string literals with catalog references, add `WriteHtmlAsync` and a `ControlIndexPage.Render(routes, commands)` pure renderer that emits an accessible, CSS/JS-free HTML5 document. Write unit tests for the renderer (derivation, no-CSS/JS tripwires, structure) plus end-to-end server tests. Update AGENTS.md.", "options": [ "Option A — Minimal-catalog approach. Create `ControlRoutes` as a small record/list alongside RouteAsync. RouteAsync continues using an if/else chain but references `ControlRoutes.All[i].Path` instead of raw `\"/health\"` strings. This is the closest to the spec: \"reference the catalog's path values.\" Lowest risk, touch the fewest lines in the router. `ControlIndexPage.Render` iterates the same catalog for the table. The test suite needs the fewest new fixtures.", "Option B — Catalog-driven dispatch. Create `ControlRoutes` that also carries a `Func<HttpListenerRequest, Task<bool>>` delegate or similar dispatch handler (or use a `Regex`-based route table with named groups). RouteAsync loops the catalog and invokes the matching handler. This eliminates the if/else chain entirely, making it impossible for a handler to exist outside the catalog. Higher churn in the router, but the strongest compile-time guarantee that the index page stays in sync with dispatch. Route dispatch logic moves into the catalog entries themselves.", "Option C — Hybrid with a helper dictionary. Create `ControlRoutes` and additionally a `Dictionary<(string Method, string Path), Func<...>>` within RouteAsync that is populated from the catalog. The if/else chain is replaced by a single dictionary lookup followed by a `not found` fallthrough. Keeps dispatch simple (no regex, no delegates in RouteInfo) while being more DRY than option A. The catalog remains a plain-data list, but the router collects it into a dictionary once at construction/start time for O(1) matching rather than O(n) if/else. `/command/{name}` and `/screenshot[?path=…]` still need a manual prefix check after the dictionary miss." ] } End your reply with a single fenced ```json block, nothing after it, matching: { "findings": string, "constraints": string[] }

## Research Findings

### Files to create

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/VisualRelay.App/Services/ControlRoutes.cs` | Static route catalog (`RouteInfo` record + `ControlRoutes.All` list) — the single source of truth for the API surface. `RouteInfo` carries `Method`, `Path` (canonical match path), `DisplayPath` (human-readable form), `Summary`. |
| `src/VisualRelay.App/Services/ControlIndexPage.cs` | Pure static `Render(IReadOnlyList<RouteInfo>, IReadOnlyList<string>)` → HTML string. No UI thread, no dependencies on Avalonia/HttpListener. HTML-encodes all interpolated values via `System.Net.WebUtility.HtmlEncode`. |
| `tests/VisualRelay.Tests/ControlIndexPageTests.cs` | Pure renderer `[Fact]` tests (derivation, no-CSS/JS tripwires, structure). If the combined test file would exceed ~300 lines, split the end-to-end round-trip tests into a second file `ControlIndexPageEndToEndTests.cs`. |

### Files to modify

| File | Lines | Changes |
|---|---|---|
| `ControlServer.Routing.cs` | 116 | (a) Add `using System.Text` (already present) and `using System.Net;` (already present). (b) Replace bare string literals (`"/health"`, `"/state"`, `"/screenshot"`, `"/command/"`) with references to `ControlRoutes.All[i].Path`. (c) Add `GET /` branch before the 404 fallthrough that calls `ControlIndexPage.Render(...)` and `WriteHtmlAsync`. (d) Add `WriteHtmlAsync` method mirroring `WriteJsonAsync` with `ContentType = "text/html; charset=utf-8"`. |
| `ControlApi.cs` | 251 | Add `public static IReadOnlyList<string> CommandNames` accessor that concatenates `IcommandNames` + `PropertyActions` (ICommand names first, then property actions). |
| `AGENTS.md` | 94 | Add `GET /` entry to the Endpoints list. |

### Key code locations

- **Route dispatch chain** — `ControlServer.Routing.cs` lines 29–56 (`RouteAsync`). Order: token gate (lines 15–24), then `/health` (29–33), `/state` (35–40), `/screenshot` (42–46), `/command/` prefix (48–52), then 404 (54–55).
- **`WriteJsonAsync`** — `ControlServer.Routing.cs` lines 109–115. Sets `ContentType = "application/json"`; `WriteHtmlAsync` will mirror this with `"text/html; charset=utf-8"`.
- **`IcommandNames`** — `ControlApi.State.cs` lines 100–105. Array of 15 strings.
- **`PropertyActions`** — `ControlApi.cs` lines 53–55. Array of 7 strings.
- **`ControlServer` constructor** — `ControlServer.cs` line 14: `ControlServer(ControlApi api, ControlServerOptions options)`.
- **`ControlApi` constructor** — `ControlApi.cs` lines 22–25: `ControlApi(MainWindowViewModel viewModel, Window window, IReadOnlyCollection<string>? confirmGatedCommands = null)`.
- **Test server setup pattern** — See `ControlServerEndToEndTests` (ControlServerTests.cs lines 62–233). Shared `HttpClient` (line 70), `GetFreePort()` (lines 226–233), `Collection("Headless")` attribute on class, `[AvaloniaFact]` per test, `server.Stop()` in `finally`.
- **`DictionaryEnvironmentAccessor`** — `TestDoubles.cs` lines 13–24. Used to inject isolated env vars in tests.
- **Json response helpers** — `ControlJson.cs`: `Json.Object(...)`, `Json.Serialize(...)`, `Json.ReadString(...)`, `Json.ReadBool(...)`.

### ControlRoutes catalog design

The catalog should contain 5 entries (matching the 5 branches in RouteAsync after adding `/`):

| Method | Path (canonical) | DisplayPath | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/` | `/` | HTML index page documenting the API surface |
| `GET` | `/health` | `/health` | Liveness check returning `{status, app}` |
| `GET` | `/state` | `/state` | Full JSON snapshot of app state and command enablement |
| `GET` | `/screenshot` | `/screenshot[?path=…]` | Capture the live window as PNG; optional file write with `?path=` |
| `POST` | `/command/` | `/command/{name}` | Invoke a named command or property action by name |

`RouteAsync` will match against `ControlRoutes.All[i].Path`: exact match for the first four, `StartsWith` for `/command/`. This satisfies the "reference the catalog's path values" requirement with minimal if/else churn (Option A from the ideation stage).

### Test strategy

- **Pure renderer tests** (plain `[Fact]`, no Avalonia): test `ControlIndexPage.Render(...)` directly.
  - Derivation: every name in `ControlApi.CommandNames` appears; every method + display path in `ControlRoutes.All` appears.
  - No-CSS tripwire: rendered HTML has no `<style`, `<link`, `stylesheet`, ` style=` (case-insensitive).
  - No-JS tripwire: rendered HTML has no `<script`, `javascript:`, or ` on[a-z]+=` (case-insensitive).
  - Structure: `<!doctype html`, `<html lang=`, `<title>`, exactly one `<h1`, `<main`, `<caption>`, `scope="col"`.
- **End-to-end round-trip tests** (`[Collection("Headless")]` + `[AvaloniaFact]`):
  - `GET /` → 200, `Content-Type` media type `text/html`, body starts with `<!doctype html`.
  - Token-configured variant: `GET /` without `X-VR-Token` → 401.
- If the combined file exceeds ~300 lines, split into `ControlIndexPageTests.cs` (pure) and `ControlIndexPageEndToEndTests.cs` (server round-trips).

### Notes

- The `ControlServer` is already `partial class` (declared on line 14 of ControlServer.cs with `public sealed partial class ControlServer`). `ControlServer.Routing.cs` uses the same `partial` pattern. No changes needed to the `partial` structure.
- `ControlApi.CommandNames` must be `public static` (not instance) so `ControlIndexPage.Render` can reference it without a `ControlApi` instance.
- The existing `IcommandNames` field is `private static readonly string[]` (line 100 of ControlApi.State.cs); `PropertyActions` is `private static readonly string[]` (line 53 of ControlApi.cs). The new accessor must be `public static IReadOnlyList<string> CommandNames` combining both.
- No new NuGet packages needed — `System.Net.WebUtility.HtmlEncode` is part of `System.Net.WebUtility` which is available in .NET 10.
